chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskan said:

I sent a question with Ibn A'yan, saying: Ask him about a eunuch who concealed his condition from a woman and had intercourse with her, and she found him to be a eunuch. He said: 'They are separated, his back is beaten, and she is entitled to the dowry due to his penetration.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if a eunuch marries a woman and conceals his condition until consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on 'Tadlis' (concealment of defects) in marriage establishes the specific legal consequences when a eunuch deceives his wife about his condition. It mandates separation, corporal punishment (being beaten on the back), and confirms the wife's right to the full dowry (mahr) due to consummation, reflecting the Shia juristic view on fraud in marital contracts.
